residents.name: Maya Chen
residents.job: Urban planner for the city transportation department
residents.personality: Organized without being rigid, observant, quietly funny, and easily absorbed in a problem. Maya likes clear surfaces and predictable mornings, but she is sentimental about small objects and keeps far too many notes.

weekly_routine.activity: Wake up, stretch, and read the news on her phone before getting dressed
Make coffee and a quick breakfast while packing lunch
Commute to the transportation department
Work from home at the glass desk, attending planning meetings and reviewing maps
Work at the city transportation department
Continue remote work and write project notes
Change clothes, put work items away, and decompress with tea
Take a brisk neighborhood walk
Practice piano scales and a few difficult passages
Cook or help prepare dinner and eat at the dining table
Read fiction and prepare clothes for the next day
Do laundry, change the bed linens, and fold clothes in the closet
Grocery shop and visit a farmers market
Clean the kitchen surfaces and organize planning papers at the desk
Make a slow breakfast and plan the coming week
Call her mother and sort personal papers

object_habits: Her reading glasses live in the upper nightstand drawer on her side of the king bed.
She places her work badge and keys on the entry console table, but often leaves a transit map there for several days.
Her work laptop stays in the left desk drawer when she works from home and goes into a canvas backpack for office days.
She keeps a small notebook and three mechanical pencils on the glass desk, aligned with the desk edge.
She puts worn-but-not-dirty sweaters on the bedroom sofa by the TV rather than back in the closet.
Her piano music is kept on the piano top under a black paperweight, even though Daniel regularly moves the pages.
She stores tea bags in the middle wide kitchen drawer and refuses to keep them in the upper cabinets because she dislikes reaching overhead.
On grocery day she leaves reusable bags on the kitchen dining table so she will not forget them.

response_habits.trigger: When a work deadline becomes uncertain or a meeting goes badly
response_habits.behavior: Takes a fast walk outside, then rewrites the problem as a short list at the glass desk

response_habits.trigger: When she is too tired to cook after commuting
response_habits.behavior: Makes toast or soup and eats at the kitchen counter instead of ordering a full meal

response_habits.trigger: When Daniel is sick or overtired
response_habits.behavior: Makes ginger tea, lowers the living-room lights, and brings the tea to the sectional

response_habits.trigger: When objects begin accumulating on shared surfaces
response_habits.behavior: Quietly gathers them into temporary piles on the coffee table and assigns each pile a destination

scheduled_stressors: Monday morning transportation-committee meetings often begin with unresolved complaints from the previous week.
Wednesday afternoon site visits involve unpredictable traffic and weather.
Thursday evening deadline reviews frequently run later than planned.
The first Saturday of each month is spent reconciling household bills and work expenses.
residents.household: Maya and Daniel are a married couple living together. They both sleep in the king bed in bedroom 1, while the queen bedroom is reserved for guests and occasional overnight work.

residents.name: Daniel Ortiz
residents.job: Audio post-production engineer for film and television
residents.personality: Warm, inventive, and sociable, with a tendency to start three tasks at once. Daniel is relaxed about clutter until it interferes with sound or cooking, and he uses humor to defuse tension. He notices tiny changes in music, appliances, and people’s voices.

weekly_routine.activity: Wake up, shower, and make coffee while listening to a podcast
Make breakfast and talk with Maya before starting work
Edit dialogue, attend remote production calls, and monitor audio
Make lunch and eat while standing at the kitchen counter
Continue audio work, sometimes joining a studio session remotely
Cook an improvised dinner using whatever needs to be used first
Work late at a post-production studio
Play digital piano arrangements or listen critically through headphones
Return home, eat something simple, and wind down quietly
Make elaborate coffee and breakfast for both of them
Buy specialty groceries and visit a music shop
Practice piano and reorganize audio equipment around the living room
Host one or two friends for drinks and dinner
Make pancakes, then clean the stovetop and counters
Take a long walk or browse records at a neighborhood shop
Watch a film with Maya from the sectional

object_habits: His headphones are almost always on the piano top, connected to the digital grand piano or resting beside it.
He leaves his phone on the bar cart when cooking and then forgets it there until someone calls.
His work laptop stays in bedroom 2 during the day, with cables spilling onto the queen bed's lower shelf when he is in a hurry.
He keeps coffee beans and a small hand grinder on the right side of the bar cabinet.
He stores spare audio adapters in the upper narrow drawer of the kitchen sink counter, despite Maya’s attempts to give them a labeled box.
He drops receipts into the left side of the entry console table and sorts them only on Sunday evening.
His house slippers migrate between the sectional and the piano stool depending on where he last listened to music.
When cooking, he sets tasting spoons on the open sink side rather than using a clean plate.

response_habits.trigger: When a client changes a project late in the day
response_habits.behavior: Puts on headphones, plays piano for ten minutes, and then returns to the work with a written priority list

response_habits.trigger: When he comes home after a late studio session
response_habits.behavior: Skips a proper dinner, drinks water, and falls asleep on the sectional before going to bed

response_habits.trigger: When Maya is irritated about his clutter
response_habits.behavior: Makes a joke first, then genuinely clears the most visible surface within the hour

response_habits.trigger: When someone in the household feels ill
response_habits.behavior: Makes broth or tea and checks repeatedly whether they need anything, even when asked not to fuss

scheduled_stressors: Wednesday and Friday studio sessions often run late because final mixes arrive at the last minute.
Tuesday morning production calls regularly include difficult clients and unclear revision notes.
Saturday dinner hosting creates a rush to shop, cook, and clear equipment from the living room.
End-of-month freelance invoices are stressful because several clients pay late.
residents.household: Maya and Daniel are a married couple living together. They both sleep in the king bed in bedroom 1, while the queen bedroom is reserved for guests and occasional overnight work.

situations.what_it_is_like: One of them comes down with a minor but exhausting illness and spends several days moving slowly, sleeping badly, and losing interest in normal routines. The sick person is frustrated by needing help and by being unable to think clearly, while the well partner becomes quietly vigilant and rearranges the day around meals, rest, and checking symptoms. Both try not to make the illness feel more dramatic than it is.
situations.what_others_notice: The sick partner is unusually quiet, less amused, and indecisive about simple things. The well partner becomes more attentive and practical, speaking softly and watching the other person's face for signs of improvement.

situations.what_it_is_like: They invite a colleague and the colleague's partner for dinner. Maya enjoys making the evening feel intentional but worries over whether everyone is comfortable; Daniel is energized by conversation and improvises when the evening takes an unexpected turn. Afterward, both are pleasantly tired and privately compare impressions of the guests.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is more animated than usual but keeps monitoring the flow of conversation. Daniel talks with his hands, tells slightly longer stories, and seems happiest when the guests laugh.

situations.what_it_is_like: A production problem keeps Daniel working far later than planned. He becomes intensely focused, then gradually silly and overtired as the pressure lifts. Maya waits up longer than she intended, irritated by the disruption but more concerned about how depleted he will be the next day.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is terse at first and then talks too quickly once he can finally explain what went wrong. Maya seems composed, but her questions become increasingly precise and her patience noticeably thinner.

situations.what_it_is_like: A major planning deadline narrows Maya's attention for several days. She thinks through problems while eating, wakes with solutions, and finds ordinary conversation harder to enter. She is not unhappy, but feels as if part of her mind is always elsewhere and is relieved when she can finally send the work away.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya becomes quieter and more exacting. She answers questions accurately but briefly, misses small jokes, and looks startled when Daniel brings her back to the immediate moment.

situations.what_it_is_like: A relative visits for a short stay, usually someone connected to Maya's family. Maya feels affectionate but responsible for preventing awkwardness, while Daniel tries to make the visitor feel included even when he is unsure what they want. The couple has less private time and becomes more aware of their different ways of hosting.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is attentive and slightly overmanaged, asking questions that sound casual but are carefully chosen. Daniel is extra warm and entertaining, though he occasionally looks to Maya for a cue about whether a joke has gone too far.

situations.what_it_is_like: Severe rain disrupts the transit network on a workday, and Maya spends the day dealing with public frustration, incomplete information, and decisions that affect thousands of strangers. She feels useful but overstimulated, carrying other people's anger long after the technical problem is under control.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya comes home mentally crowded and unusually observant of every sound and delay. She recounts the day in a calm voice, but her shoulders stay tense and she has little patience for vague complaints.

situations.what_it_is_like: Maya commits to learning a difficult piano piece she has admired for years. At first she feels embarrassed by how slowly she improves, then becomes absorbed in small gains and starts using practice as a way to clear her mind. The project gives her a private source of pleasure outside work.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya becomes more patient with repetition and occasionally hums without realizing it. Daniel notices her frustration when a passage resists her, but also sees a rare, unguarded satisfaction when she gets through it.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel accepts a short freelance project alongside his regular employment. He likes the creative control and extra money but underestimates how much of his attention it will consume. He feels proud when the work is good and guilty when it makes him less available at home.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is more buoyant when discussing the project and more distracted in ordinary conversation. Maya sees him trying to appear relaxed while mentally dividing every evening into tasks.

situations.what_it_is_like: A neighborhood power outage interrupts an ordinary evening. Maya initially feels thrown off by the loss of structure, while Daniel treats it as an invitation to improvise. After the first hour, they settle into an unexpectedly calm night and enjoy being released from their usual obligations.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is restless and keeps estimating when normal life will resume. Daniel becomes playful and conversational, taking pleasure in the unusual quiet and gently teasing Maya for trying to organize it.

situations.what_it_is_like: Maya has a painful disagreement with a close friend about loyalty and communication. She replays the conversation, drafts several possible messages, and struggles to decide whether clarity or kindness should come first. Daniel cannot solve it for her, which makes his steady presence more valuable than advice.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is present but inward, with long pauses before she answers. Daniel notices that she becomes unusually self-critical and responds by listening carefully rather than filling the silence.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel has a long call with a family member who needs reassurance or practical help. He begins warmly, becomes progressively more involved, and ends the call carrying concerns he cannot immediately fix. He feels responsible for staying easygoing even when the conversation leaves him worried.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel's voice becomes gentler and more patient than usual. Afterward he seems distracted and makes jokes that do not quite land, while Maya can tell he wants company without wanting to discuss the call yet.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel attempts an ambitious recipe after seeing it in a video or hearing about it from a friend. He enjoys the sensory problem-solving but loses track of time and portions. Maya starts skeptical, becomes interested when the method proves clever, and is willing to forgive a messy process if the result is genuinely good.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is absorbed, talkative, and unwilling to admit that he is improvising. Maya hovers at the edge of the activity, offering precise comments that sound critical until Daniel realizes she is actually invested.

situations.what_it_is_like: One of them needs uninterrupted work space while the other is also home. They negotiate boundaries more formally than either likes, trying to protect concentration without making the shared home feel divided. By evening, both are hungry for ordinary conversation and slightly resentful of how much coordination work the day required.
situations.what_others_notice: The working person becomes hard to reach and reacts strongly to interruptions. The other resident grows careful and quiet, then noticeably more expressive once the workday is declared finished.

situations.what_it_is_like: They attend a neighborhood gathering where Maya knows only a few people and Daniel quickly starts conversations with strangers. Maya enjoys observing the social patterns but tires sooner; Daniel feels restored by the easy contact and wants to stay longer. They leave after negotiating a compromise that satisfies neither completely but becomes funny on the walk home.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is courteous, watchful, and quietly amused by the crowd. Daniel is open and energetic, collecting small stories about people they may never see again.

situations.what_it_is_like: Daniel's production schedule shifts later for several weeks. He has more energy at night but feels disconnected from Maya's mornings and misses the ease of sharing the same daily rhythm. Maya tries to protect their overlap without turning every evening into a scheduled appointment.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is alert when Maya is winding down and sluggish when she is ready to talk before work. Maya becomes more deliberate about asking for time together and more visibly disappointed when their timing fails.

situations.what_it_is_like: A senior colleague unexpectedly praises Maya's judgment in a meeting. She feels pleased but suspicious of praise that arrives without a request attached. Over the next day she privately revisits the words, allowing herself to believe them only gradually.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya seems lighter and more willing to tell a story from work. She downplays the compliment while clearly hoping Daniel will understand that it mattered.

situations.what_it_is_like: A crucial piece of Daniel's professional equipment fails shortly before a delivery. He becomes intensely practical, calling favors and reconstructing the work under pressure. Once the crisis is solved, the delayed fear arrives all at once and leaves him drained.
situations.what_others_notice: Daniel is focused and unusually silent, with a clipped professional manner. Afterward he is affectionate but exhausted, laughing at minor inconveniences because the serious problem has finally passed.

situations.what_it_is_like: They review household spending and upcoming expenses together. Maya wants categories, trends, and decisions; Daniel wants the conversation to remain connected to the life they are trying to enjoy. The discussion is usually calm but reveals their different definitions of prudence.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya becomes analytical and keeps returning to specifics. Daniel is cooperative until he feels judged, then becomes humorous or defensive before making a sincere effort to engage.

situations.what_it_is_like: They attend a memorial for someone important to a friend. Both are affected, though in different ways: Maya focuses on the details of the person's life and the needs of the mourners, while Daniel is struck by voices, silences, and remembered stories. They are subdued afterward and more physically affectionate than usual.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya appears composed until a small detail breaks through her control. Daniel speaks less, listens closely, and seeks Maya's hand or shoulder without making a point of it.

situations.what_it_is_like: A change in Maya's assignment gives her a different commute and a more demanding morning schedule. She initially resents losing unhurried time, then begins noticing new patterns in the city that feed her professional curiosity. The household has to adapt to her leaving earlier and returning with a different kind of fatigue.
situations.what_others_notice: Maya is more purposeful in the morning and more mentally full at night. Daniel notices that she has new observations to share, even when she is too tired to tell them in a polished way.

small_disturbances.text: A call from her mother arrives during a concentrated work period and leaves Maya distracted afterward.
A package arrives earlier than expected, and Daniel cannot remember which order it belongs to.
They discover they have run out of milk just as one of them begins making breakfast.
A client sends a message marked urgent that turns out to be vague and nonurgent.
A transit alert changes her morning route after she has already planned the timing.
The doorbell rings for a neighbor's delivery, and neither resident recognizes the name.
He realizes he has left an important personal appointment off his calendar.
She finds a note she wrote to herself but cannot remember what the abbreviated reminder means.
A smoke alarm chirps once and then stops, making them listen for it throughout the evening.
A friend calls to ask for advice, but mostly needs Daniel to listen for half an hour.
A colleague asks for a quick favor that expands into an unexpected hour of work.
They disagree about whether a faint unfamiliar sound is coming from an appliance or outside.
He discovers that a subscription renewal has charged more than he expected.
She receives a calendar invitation with the wrong time zone and has to untangle the meeting details.
A sudden rainstorm catches one of them away from home without suitable clothing.
He starts telling Maya a story and loses the thread because another idea occurs to him.
She notices that a familiar neighborhood business has closed and spends the evening thinking about the change.
A guest cancels at the last minute, leaving the couple to decide whether to keep the planned meal.
